comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implementation plan (worktree xenops-fold-race, based on Gerrit 1771 PS2 for doctor shapes; will push WIP until 1771 merges):

1. compact_txn.py — absorbing re-fold semantics: a new fold-input partition helper identifies the latest LIVE snapshot among candidates and its source_event_uuids. (a) When the snapshot itself folds, the reducer's event_files_override is ORDERED as [pre-snapshot cited files, snapshot, orphans by ts, post-snapshot files] so an orphan (pre-snapshot ts, uuid not cited) replays ON TOP of the snapshot — pinned semantics: snapshot, then orphans by ts, then post-snapshot events. The new snapshot cites the orphan uuids, clearing ORPHAN_EVENT. (b) SAFETY GUARD discovered during design: if the live snapshot is within the horizon (young) while pre-snapshot files are foldable, folding those pre-snapshot files ALONE would write a new pre-snapshot SNAPSHOT that the governing snapshot then positionally skips — silently burying the orphan for good. Such pre-snapshot candidates are DEFERRED from the fold until the snapshot itself is foldable. (c) Retired files are never candidates and a live file cited in source_event_uuids is never re-absorbed (replay skips it by uuid; it is re-cited, not re-applied).

2. compact.py — new --absorb-orphans flag: bypasses ONLY the "remote SNAPSHOT exists" refusal (which stays for plain rebar compact); sync-before-compact still runs.

3. doctor.py (on 1771 shapes) — read-only scan_orphans() emits ORPHAN_EVENT findings (per ticket, path list); doctor --repair routes them AFTER dirty-tracker repair: reuse 1771's _dirty_backup_ref (refs/rebar-doctor/<utc-ts>) before mutation — no backup ref, no mutation — then per-ticket absorbing re-fold via compact_cli([tid, --threshold=0, --horizon=0, --absorb-orphans]); compact takes the store write lock itself (run_repair holds none, same as the dirty path).

TDD: oracle tests first (race reproduction: fold with the late comment file absent, then materialize it as the union merge would; assert show misses it + ORPHAN_EVENT flagged; then repair => visible + clean), ordering pin (orphan appends after snapshot-absorbed comments, before post-snapshot ones), defer guard, refusal-stays guard, no-reabsorption guards, doctor backup-ref + no-backup-no-mutation. Then implement to green; manual mutation pass targeting absorb-flag inversion, skipped backup ref, dropped source_event_uuids check, ordering swap, retired re-absorption.

comments.body:
Implementation complete (TDD, all green). What landed:

1. compact_txn.py — absorbing re-fold semantics. New helpers along existing seams:
   _is_snapshot_path, _defer_presnapshot_foldables (f96b safety guard: pre-snapshot
   candidates NEVER fold without their governing snapshot — folding them alone would
   write a pre-snapshot SNAPSHOT the governing one positionally buries), and
   _ordered_fold_input (PINNED order: snapshots first, then all other candidates by
   timestamp — so a pre-snapshot late arrival replays ON TOP of the snapshot and the
   next snapshot cites it). _compact_locked now always reduces over that pinned
   override; _select_fold_set extracts the partition+guard (complexity ratchet green,
   new=0 increased=0).

2. compact.py — --absorb-orphans flag: bypasses ONLY the remote-SNAPSHOT refusal;
   sync-before-compact still runs; plain compact still refuses. Arg loop extracted to
   _parse_compact_flags (compact_cli was at C901=15 ceiling).

3. doctor.py — extends change 1771's shapes (based on refs/changes/71/1771/2):
   scan_orphans (read-only, reuses fsck_scan._check_snapshot so the doors cannot
   drift; kind=ORPHAN_EVENT with paths), _repair_orphans (backup ref via the shared
   _dirty_backup_ref BEFORE any mutation — no ref, no mutation; routes each damaged
   ticket to compact --absorb-orphans --threshold=0 --horizon=0; no outer lock —
   compact self-locks), _repair_store_level ordering: dirty first, then orphans, then
   link repairs.

Guards: a retired event is never a fold candidate (not *.json); a live event already
cited in source_event_uuids is uuid-skipped by replay — re-cited at most, never
re-applied (test pins both).

Tests: tests/unit/test_fold_race_orphan_absorb.py — 11 tests, RED-first verified
(8 failed pre-impl for the right reasons), now 11/11 green. Race reproduced
deterministically: hide the late comment file, fold, land it back committed as the
union merge would; assert show misses it + fsck ORPHAN_EVENT; then absorb/doctor
repair -> visible, fsck clean, backup ref present. Ordering pinned:
[c0, c1, middle(orphan), after].

Mutation pass (manual, 6 mutants, ALL KILLED): absorb-flag inversion (3 tests fail),
skipped/faked backup ref (2), ordering swap orphans-before-snapshot (6), defer-guard
removal (1), snapshot-predicate broken (7), doctor orphan-filter broken (2).

Validation: make lint green (ruff+format+ratchet active=53 new=0 increased=0),
make typecheck green (mypy 539 files), tests/unit -k "compact or doctor or fsck":
146 passed, 4 skipped.

Discovered+guarded latent hazard (the defer guard above): before this change a
re-fold could bury an orphan under a pre-snapshot SNAPSHOT silently and permanently
— now deferred until the governing snapshot ages out of the horizon.

Next: commit + push to Gerrit as WIP (1771 unmerged at last check).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INVESTIGATION (per operator hold): ADR-0035 + fsck_repair.py + rebuild path, vs the
xenops plan. Findings:

(a) IS THE LIVE INCIDENT COVERED BY THE EXISTING DOOR? YES. The observed orphan is a
COMMENT — in _AUTO_RECOVER_ORPHAN_TYPES (fsck_repair.py:38). Both fsck doors reach a
full-log rebuild that captures it: (1) fsck --repair-snapshots -> repair_or_plan ->
rebuild_with_restore -> rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log (reduce include_retired=True,
snapshots stripped, no positional short-circuit; crash-safe .snapshot-rebuild.bak
sentinel; b636 fail-closed guard when a prior snapshot cites sources absent from
disk); (2) fsck --repair (A3 cluster) -> _repair_ticket, which routes BY TYPE:
auto-recover -> rebuild, order-sensitive -> human triage, never auto-written. The
new snapshot cites the orphan; fsck goes clean. The refuted premise is confirmed
refuted: "no repair door" was wrong.

(b) ACTUAL GAPS FOUND:

G1 (SERIOUS, and the real bug worth a ticket): the NATURAL RE-FOLD DESTROYS
ORPHANS. On origin/main, a compaction whose candidate set contains [orphan,
snapshot] (sweep via --skip-sync, compact-on-close, or once foldable live events
cross the threshold) reduces via whole-dir replay -> positional skip buries the
orphan's EFFECT, yet source_uuids includes the orphan's uuid and the file is
retired. Result: the effect is permanently lost AND the ORPHAN_EVENT signal is
erased (uuid now cited -> fsck clean). The window between orphan creation and the
next natural fold is the ONLY time the existing door can fire. Verified by my RED
test run: refold rc=0, comment still invisible, file retired, uuid cited. ADR-0035
Option 3 prevents new orphans at fold time but does not protect an
already-landed orphan from the NEXT fold.

G2: doctor --repair does not route ORPHAN_EVENT anywhere (merged 1771 state: links
+ dirty + locks only). The heal is reachable only via the separate fsck flags.
Cosmetic-to-moderate: two operator doors, one blind to this class.

G3: nothing AUTO-triggers detection or heal on the writer path after a union
merge. sync only HINTS at fsck on conflict; ensure_fresh and the compact trigger do
no orphan scanning. Detection waits for a human/external watchdog to run fsck.
Note G1 makes this worse: waiting silently converts repairable damage into
unrepairable loss.

G4 (policy drift between the two existing fsck doors): --repair-snapshots'
repair_or_plan triggers on ANY ORPHAN_EVENT finding and rebuilds whole-ticket
WITHOUT the type routing; --repair enforces auto-recover vs human-triage. The
routing discipline exists on one door only (possibly intentional as an explicit
opt-in, but worth confirming).

(c) ORDERING: YES, MOOT — full-log rebuild replays the complete raw log in HLC
filename total order, so an absorbed orphan takes effect AT ITS TIMESTAMP position;
deterministic and equal to what a clone that had always seen the event computes.
That is the canonical semantics. My change 1779's pinned "snapshot state, then
orphans by ts" ordering CONTRADICTS it (e.g. orphan ts between c0 and c1: rebuild
yields [c0, middle, c1, c2]; 1779 yields [c0, c1, middle, ...]) — two repair doors
would produce different states from identical bytes. 1779 also absorbs ALL types
blindly, bypassing the triage routing — the exact hazard the routing guards.

DISPOSITION OF CHANGE 1779: marked WIP (done, REST 200). Its doctor/--absorb-orphans
door duplicates the existing repair and must not land as-is. Two pieces remain
genuinely useful if the ticket is rewritten to G1: (i) the defer guard
(pre-snapshot candidates never fold without their governing snapshot — closes a
silent-burial hazard adjacent to G1); (ii) making the fold orphan-AWARE — but the
correct shape is likely: fold EXCLUDES un-cited pre-snapshot events from
fold_files/source_uuids (leaving them live so the fsck signal and repair window
survive), rather than absorbing with novel ordering. Absorption, if wanted at fold
time, should reuse full-log-total-order semantics and respect the type routing.

Recommend: rewrite the ticket to G1 (fold must not destroy orphan evidence), with
G2/G3/G4 as separate follow-up candidates. I will rework or abandon 1779 to match.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Rewritten after premise refutation (see comments): the observed fold-horizon race (bridge write + concurrent compact → union merge lands an event timestamped before the snapshot, absent from `source_event_uuids`) is the known RC2 class of ADR-0035, and the repair door EXISTS and works: `rebar fsck --repair-snapshots` / `fsck --repair` → `compact.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` (full HLC-ordered log incl. `.retired`, `.snapshot-rebuild.bak` sentinel, fail-closed guard) — it healed the live incident on e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2.

The REAL defect (verified in a RED run against current main): **the next natural fold LAUNDERS the orphan.** When a ticket with an un-cited pre-snapshot event crosses the compaction threshold, the fold's whole-dir enumeration RETIRES the orphan file and CITES its uuid in the new snapshot's `source_event_uuids` — but the replay's positional skip means its effect is NOT in the compiled state. fsck then reports clean (uuid cited, file retired): repairable damage silently becomes unrepairable-by-tooling loss at the first threshold crossing after the race. The existing repair door only works in the window BEFORE that fold. Secondary gap: (G4) `fsck --repair-snapshots` rebuilds on ANY orphan type, bypassing the `_AUTO_RECOVER` vs `_HUMAN_TRIAGE` routing that `fsck --repair` enforces (fsck_repair.py:38-41, applied at :202).

## Proposed fix
1. **Stop the laundering (G1, the bug):** the natural fold (compact_txn) must EXCLUDE orphans from both retirement and `source_event_uuids` citation. The exclusion predicate is exactly fsck's orphan definition (fsck_scan.py:373-386), anchored to a PRIOR snapshot already present in the fold set: an active event whose filename sorts before an existing folded-in SNAPSHOT's filename AND whose uuid is absent from THAT snapshot's `source_event_uuids`. Extract/reuse that predicate as a shared helper so fold and fsck cannot disagree. On a first fold (no prior SNAPSHOT in the dir) the predicate matches nothing and every event folds normally — the new snapshot's own citation list (which the fold is building) plays no role in the predicate. An excluded orphan stays an unretired, un-cited file, so the fsck ORPHAN_EVENT finding and the repair window survive indefinitely. The fold does NOT absorb orphans itself (that would bypass the type routing); it defers to the repair door. Ordering note: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` replays the full log in HLC total order, so absorbed order-sensitive events are deterministic there — no new ordering semantics are introduced by this change.
2. **Routing parity (G4):** `--repair-snapshots` applies the same `_AUTO_RECOVER`/`_HUMAN_TRIAGE` routing instead of rebuilding unconditionally, so the two fsck repair paths cannot disagree about order-sensitive orphans.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py — fold enumeration excludes un-cited pre-snapshot events from retirement + citation (defer guard).
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py — routing parity for --repair-snapshots (the `_AUTO_RECOVER_ORPHAN_TYPES`/`_HUMAN_TRIAGE_ORPHAN_TYPES` split already applied by `fsck --repair` at fsck_repair.py:202).
- tests/unit/test_fold_orphan_laundering.py — new: RED reproduction of the laundering (orphan retired+cited+effect-lost today), exclusion behavior, repair-window survival across a threshold-crossing fold.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A ticket with an un-cited pre-snapshot COMMENT that crosses the compaction threshold keeps the orphan unretired/un-cited and fsck still reports ORPHAN_EVENT after the fold; `fsck --repair-snapshots` afterward restores the comment to `show`; integration test.
- [ ] A first fold of a ticket with NO prior snapshot folds every event normally (nothing excluded); a re-fold of a healthy ticket whose prior snapshot cites all pre-snapshot events likewise excludes nothing; guard tests.
- [ ] `--repair-snapshots` no longer rebuilds past `_HUMAN_TRIAGE` types; guard test.
- [ ] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.

## Out of scope
**Already-laundered snapshots (historical damage):** folds that happened BEFORE this fix retired+cited orphans without applying their effect; fsck reports those tickets clean. The data is still recoverable — retired files are preserved and `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` replays the full log including `.retired` — but DETECTION requires an expensive full-log-vs-snapshot state comparison, filed as follow-up `trainsick-fleeting-avocet` (2aaf-90b9-4a31-43bf, linked discovered_from). Known live incidents: one (e27c, healed before any fold crossed it). Writer-path auto-detection after union merge (G3 — separate follow-up if wanted); doctor-side ORPHAN_EVENT routing (doctor.py has no snapshot/orphan scan — orphan detection and repair are fsck's domain via fsck_repair.py, and adding a duplicate scan to doctor would be a parallel implementation; users are directed to `fsck --repair`); bridge/Jira duplicate policy; crash-atomicity (mantis, landed); dirty-tree repair (dormouse, landed).
